newsitem.title: UK: Heathrow rail cargo consortium seeks EU funding.
newsitem.headline: Heathrow rail cargo consortium seeks EU funding.

text.p: A consortium planning to develop a 100 million stg rail freight terminal of up to 250 acres near London Heathrow Airport is planning to apply for "substantial" funding for the project from the EU, its consultant and main promoter Rod Hilditch said.
He told Reuters that an application for an EU "Pilot Action Combined Transport" (PACT) grant would be made by the consortium - named FOCAL (Freight Operators' Commercial Access Link) - next month.
He said he thought that a grant of up to 10 million stg to cover feasibility and pilot studies, equipment purchasing and the provision of infrastructure could possibly be forthcoming.
Hilditch said the project, if it goes ahead, could remove about five percent of goods traffic from the highly congested M25 motorway circling London and switch it to rail transportation.
The consortium, he said, comprises freight operators and distribution companies, which he declined to name.
English, Welsh and Scottish Railway told Reuters it is one of the companies backing the scheme.

The plan is to establish the proposed new rail freight terminal near Heathrow at the junction of the M4 and M25 motorways to connect with the Great Western main line between Paddington and Bristol and also to provide a link for airfreight to and from the Channel Tunnel and ports including Southampton.
"Any EU funding would be cream on the cake but, regardless, we would expect the project to go ahead anyway," said Hilditch.

He said that a planning application for the project would be submitted to the UK Department of Transport and an application to build an intermodal freight village lodged with Slough borough and Berkshire county councils by June 1.

Hilditch said that if all went well, work on the site could begin in 1998 and the proposed rail connections could be in place by the turn of the century, although the planned freight village would probably not be ready by then.
